description: Tradovate JavaScript indicator (build-order step 7): a THIN renderer that reads a levels file and draws EXACTLY the 5 lines + regime readout and nothing else -- Call Wall, Put Wall, 0DTE Call Wall, 0DTE Put Wall (each a single horizontal line at its strike, labeled with strike, $GEX/1%, and WEAK/MODERATE/STRONG/EXTREME), plus a neutral gray Gamma Flip line, plus a small 'TOTAL: +/- / 0DTE: +/-' regime readout. It renders on the MNQ chart. It must NOT compute GEX and must NOT draw OI/IV/greeks/MaxPain/full-chain/distance-to-level, order flow, or volume profiles (those are manual). Replay must show the levels known as of the replayed timestamp (no look-ahead): when the user clicks a replay date/time the indicator loads the matching point-in-time levels file. Includes a level-file loader shim since a Tradovate custom indicator can read a fed file/data source (this is why Tradovate was chosen over TradingView).
steps: Create the indicator under a new top-level dir, e.g. tradovate/gamma_map_indicator.js. Implement it as a Tradovate custom indicator following Tradovate's indicator API shape (init/map/plots or the documented custom-indicator structure). Since exact Tradovate API details may need confirmation, structure the code so the levels-parsing + line/label/regime logic is pure and unit-testable, with the Tradovate-specific drawing calls isolated in a thin adapter section clearly commented as the integration point.

Parse the levels JSON produced by FEAT-005 (the {walls, flip, regime, provenance} schema). Render 5 horizontal lines at the MNQ prices: 4 walls + gamma flip. Style: walls solid with side-appropriate emphasis, flip neutral gray/dotted. Each wall label shows 'LABEL  <strike>  $<gex>B / 1%  <STRENGTH>' matching the example block in build-spec SS9a. Regime readout: small 'TOTAL: NEGATIVE  0DTE: NEGATIVE' text.

Replay/no-look-ahead: the indicator selects the levels file whose asof is the latest <= the chart's current replay timestamp, never a future one. Document how the file is fed to the indicator (Tradovate data feed / hosted JSON), and keep a clear seam for the level source.

If a wall/flip is missing or a chain was a volume proxy, surface it minimally (e.g. a 'proxy' suffix on the regime readout) rather than drawing a misleadingly authoritative line; never present proxy walls as classic OI-GEX.

Add a JS unit test (or a small Node test harness) OR, if a JS test runner is not set up, a Python test that loads the same levels JSON and asserts the render-model the JS would build (line count = 5, labels formatted per SS9a, regime string correct). Prefer a lightweight Node test if node is available; otherwise validate the pure formatting logic by mirroring it in a tested Python helper is NOT acceptable -- instead extract the JS formatting into functions and test them with node --test if node exists. Check `node --version` in a single bash call; if node is absent, add a self-contained JS assertion script run via node, and if node is entirely unavailable mark this sub-check as an environment limitation in findings and validate the JSON contract via a Python test instead.

Write tradovate/README.md documenting: what the indicator draws (the 5 lines + regime, nothing else), how to install it as a Tradovate custom indicator on the MNQ chart, how the levels file is fed, and the replay behavior.
Commit on nuke_root: 'feat: Tradovate JS indicator -- thin 5-line + regime renderer with replay no-look-ahead'.
acceptance_criteria: The indicator renders exactly 5 lines (4 walls + gamma flip) and the TOTAL/0DTE regime readout, and nothing else (no OI/IV/greeks/MaxPain/full-chain/distance/order-flow/volume-profile).
Wall labels are formatted per the build-spec SS9a example (label, strike, $GEX/1%, strength band).
The renderer reads the FEAT-005 levels JSON schema and selects the levels file at-or-before the replay timestamp (no look-ahead).
A test (node --test if node is available, else a JSON-contract test) verifies the render model: 5 lines, correct labels, correct regime string.
tradovate/README.md documents install-on-MNQ, level feeding, and replay behavior.
verification: export PYENV_ROOT="/root/.pyenv" && export PATH="$PYENV_ROOT/shims:$PYENV_ROOT/bin:$PATH" && (node --version && node --test tradovate/ 2>&1 | tail -20) || (pyenv global 3.11.15 && PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/test_indicator_contract.py -q)
